entries.actualCapability: Return TrenchBroom MCP bridge status and active document summary.
Diagnose MCP bridge configuration, mode, local trust, and tool availability.
List documents currently opened in TrenchBroom.
Open a map document by absolute path.
Open, activate, and verify a map document before returning success.
Activate an open document by document index or path.
Save an open document. Transient documents require an absolute path.
Save the active document. Alias of documents_save for automated MCP flows; use expectedDocumentPath to guard the active map before saving.
Save the active document to an absolute path. Alias of documents_save with path and optional expectedDocumentPath guard.
Close an open document. Dirty documents require discardChanges=true.
Export an open document to a map file by absolute path.
Return metadata for the active document.
Return a compact map summary for the active document.
Search entities, brushes, and properties in the active map.
Return the current editor selection.

Inspect the current editor selection with compact summaries by default. Use detail=full or includeProperties=true to read selected entity key/value properties such as targetname, target, origin, angles, and custom fields.

Inspect entity key/value links in the active map without reading the .map file. Defaults to the current selected entity as the start and follows targetname -> target style links. Reports missing links, duplicate names, and cycles instead of guessing.
Set the current editor selection using MCP object ids.
Filter map objects by type, classname, targetname, material, bounds, or text.
Select leaf selectable objects whose logical bounds intersect or fit inside a box. Defaults exclude world/container matches.
Grow the current node selection to parents, children, or siblings.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. For normal Agent review, use render_review_current_scene(scope:"selection"), render_review_selector, or module_render_review instead.
Clear MCP overlay markers, optionally clearing the editor selection.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only; use geometry review tools instead of live UI layout inspection.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only; geometry review tools now provide deterministic saved review bundles without changing the live UI layout.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only; use render_review_selector or module_render_review view presets instead of controlling the live editor camera.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only; use render_review_selector or module_render_review view presets instead of controlling the live editor camera.
List executable TrenchBroom actions for the current context.
Execute a TrenchBroom action by id if it is enabled in the current context.
Set MCP overlay labels or highlighted object ids.
Clear MCP overlay state.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only; use render_review_current_scene, render_review_selector, or render_review_operation for Agent scene review.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only; use render_review_selector, render_review_operation, or module_render_review.
Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only; use render_review_selector, render_review_operation, or module_render_review.

Retired lightweight-runtime viewport helper. Searchable for migration only. For normal Agent self-review, use geometry review tools such as render_review_selector, render_review_operation, render_review_current_scene, or module_render_review.

Low-level geometry review renderer used by higher-level review tools. Prefer render_review_selector, render_review_operation, or render_review_current_scene unless you already have explicit objectIds/operationIds and need direct control.

Create a compact Agent-readable geometry review for the active document in one call. The tool automatically reviews current brush geometry, chooses terrain-friendly defaults when appropriate, writes a contact_sheet.png, and returns a small summary with preferredCapturePath. Use detail=full for captures, quality arrays, and other manifest details. renderReadable only checks render output readability; qualityValid is a legacy alias, not semantic geometry validation. Human or skill review must judge whether the image matches the requested scene intent.

Create an isolated Agent-readable geometry review bundle for generated scene objects. Pass operationIds or objectIds; the CPU renderer draws only target geometry with whitebox faces and strong outlines, avoiding live viewport layout/visibility changes. renderReadable only checks render output readability; qualityValid is a legacy alias, not semantic geometry validation. Human or skill review must judge whether the image matches the requested scene intent.

Preview a structured JSON selector against the active map. Selectors can combine session metadata, moduleId, operation ids, type, bounds, material, classname, targetname, and text query. idsMode=count returns counts only; idsMode=sample adds small object summaries.
Replace the current selection with objects matched by a structured JSON selector. Use this to recover generated modules without carrying long object id lists.
Delete live objects matched by a structured JSON selector in one transaction. This is safer than pasting a long objectIds array when the target was tagged with moduleId/part/role metadata.

Render an isolated geometry review for objects matched by a structured JSON selector. This composes selector_preview with render_review_targets and keeps the MCP response compact. renderReadable only checks render output readability; qualityValid is a legacy alias, not semantic geometry validation. Human or skill review must judge whether the image matches the requested scene intent.

List session-level modules discovered from metadata.moduleId and IR/module registry records. Modules are MCP-session only and are not written to the map. Defaults to live modules only so stale modules from previous documents do not pollute Agent target recovery.
Inspect one session-level module by moduleId, including live/stale object counts, operation ids, metadata, and bounds.
Select all live objects in a session-level module.

Render an isolated review bundle for a session-level module. By default the selector limit is raised to cover the full live module; pass limit only when you intentionally want a partial review. renderReadable only checks render output readability; qualityValid is a legacy alias, not semantic geometry validation. Human or skill review must judge whether the image matches the requested scene intent.
Validate a session-level module's live objects and optional route continuity. This reports geometry facts only; skill/domain logic decides gameplay or aesthetic quality.
Remove stale session metadata/object references for one module. This cleans MCP session state only and does not modify the map or undo stack.
Create an entity in the active document.
Update entity key/value properties.
Batch update entity key/value properties by objectIds or operationIds. Prefer this over deleting and recreating entities for key cleanup.
Batch delete entity property keys by objectIds or operationIds.
Delete an entity, brush, patch, group, or layer node.
List entity classes from the active game entity definitions.
Return FGD schema details for one entity classname.
Create an entity using FGD defaults plus supplied properties.

Create a point entity after checking the active FGD schema supports the classname. This is the preferred one-step helper over manually calling fgd_entities_list, entity_schema, and entity_create_from_schema.
Create multiple point entities after validating each classname against the active FGD schema. Use this for lights, spawns, and route markers that should land in one undoable transaction.
Tie selected or specified brushes to a brush entity.
Move brushes out of brush entities back to the world or current parent.
List brush primitive types supported by MCP.
List generic convex footprint grammars for route-aware polygon platforms.
Create a brush primitive using a type parameter.
Create a box brush in the active document.
Create many box brushes in one transaction. Prefer this for platform chains, jump blocks, and other repeated cuboids instead of many brush_create_box calls.

Create many convex prism platforms from 2D polygons in one transaction. Prefer this for diamond, trapezoid, chamfered, and route-guiding platforms instead of box-only chains. Invalid batches fail before mutation and return polygonDiagnostics with failing point/edge indices for every invalid polygon.
Create a wedge brush in the active document.
Create a cylinder brush in the active document.
Create a cone brush in the active document.
Create a hollow cylinder from multiple convex brushes.
Create a UV or ico sphere brush.
Create a square pyramid brush.
Create a tetrahedron brush inside the given bounds.
Create one expert brush from plane point triples.
Create one convex vertical prism from a 2D polygon and Z range.
Create one convex annular cylinder-sector brush.
Create an arch brush primitive. Listed as unsupported until a stable native arch generator is exposed.

entries.actualCapability: Create a torus brush primitive. Listed as unsupported because BSP brushes cannot represent it as a single convex brush.
entries.placeholderReason: The baseline catalog declares this capability but no implementation behavior was present for migration.

entries.actualCapability: Hidden diagnostic timeline for the active bridge session, including creation time and live/stale object counts when a document is active. Prefer history_status for normal Agent workflow and operation_inspect for a specific operation.
Return compact MCP operation history availability diagnostics for the active bridge session and document.
Inspect an MCP operation by operationId. Use detail=summary by default and detail=ids/full only when object ids or debug data are needed. Includes live/stale status when a document is active.

Hidden manual recovery helper that selects live map objects created or changed by an MCP operation. Prefer selector_preview, module_inspect, render_review_operation, or operation_inspect unless a human explicitly needs the native selection changed.
Return generic validation status for an MCP operation. Defaults to compact summary diagnostics; use detail=full to include per-object diagnostics.
Undo the latest MCP operation if it is still on top of the native undo stack.
Undo MCP operations from the latest operation back to and including the given operationId. Stops with structured diagnostics if the native undo stack no longer matches the expected MCP transaction.
Redo the latest MCP operation undone by history_undo_mcp.
Search GoldSrc model, sprite, and sound assets using the unified asset browser rules.
Create a point entity for a .mdl asset.
Create a point entity for a .spr asset.
Create an ambient_generic entity for a .wav asset.
List loaded materials in the active document. With an empty query, returns the first N materials plus currentMaterial and fallbackMaterial.

Search loaded materials in the active document. If no material matches, use fallbackMaterial from the result for safe blockout geometry. Returns detailed results plus materials/materialNames aliases for simple agent consumption.
Return current texture lock and UV lock state for modeling operations.
Set texture lock and/or UV lock for subsequent modeling operations.

Apply a material to selected faces, target objects, operation targets, or a semantic subset such as top/bottom/side faces. Result reports whether the requested material exists in the loaded material set.

Apply a material to brushes matched by a safe selection_filter-style query. The tool only edits brush faces and ignores world/group/layer parents. It also accepts objectIds or operationIds as direct targets, then can narrow by faceSemantic or normal. Result reports materialExists and a fallbackMaterial when the requested material is not loaded.
Replace one material with another on selected faces/brushes or the whole map. Result reports find/replace material existence.
Apply a basic UV alignment mode to a face or face selection.
Copy material and UV attributes from one face to selected or specified target faces.
List faces for one brush, selected brushes, or all selected brush faces.
Select one or more brush faces.
Set face material and basic UV attributes for selected or specified faces.
Delete one or more entity, brush, patch, group, or layer nodes.

Expert destructive helper that deletes selectable objects matched by a safe selection_filter-style query. Defaults exclude node:world, require selectable matches, and remove redundant descendants before deleting. Prefer structured selector_preview followed by objects_delete_by_selector for generated MCP content.

Compatibility helper that deletes the live selectable objects changed by a previous MCP operation. Prefer structured selector/module deletion for current workflows; use this only when an operation id is the clearest target.

Transform one or more selectable objects using translate, rotate, or scale. Prefer selector targets for module/route/part iteration so generated scene pieces can be stretched, moved, or rotated without deleting and rebuilding them. If objectIds, operationIds, and selector are omitted, transforms the current user selection.

Create a native TrenchBroom group from the current user selection. Groups are for visible Outliner organization and user selection convenience; keep semantic tracking in module/metadata/selector records.

Inspect native TrenchBroom group structure by objectId/objectIds or by current selected group. Returns group name, bounds, child counts, edit state, and linked group summary. This does not read or write semantic metadata.
Rename the currently selected native TrenchBroom group or groups. The current selection must contain only groups.
Ungroup the currently selected native TrenchBroom groups and leave their former children selected. Use for organization cleanup, not semantic metadata changes.
Validate the active map and return compact passed/count/recoveryAction problem counts by default.
Return map validation problems with passed/recoveryAction and safe quick fix metadata. Each problem includes a line-sensitive id for problems_fix and a stableKey for before/after comparison.
Apply one safe quick fix to selected validation problem ids.
Apply all currently available safe validation quick fixes.
List compilation profiles for the active document.
Run a compilation profile through TrenchBroom's existing compile dialog.
Return recent text from the current compile dialog output.
Load a compiler pointfile (.pts/.lin) into the active document.
Create multiple blockout operations in one transaction. Prefer this over many atomic brush_create calls for architectural generation.

Legacy script bridge that runs local Python source and compiles returned Blockout IR through blockout_create_batch. Prefer skill recipe scripts that write IR files, then use ir_compile_preview_from_file and ir_apply_from_file.
Import a local grayscale image as brush terrain. Defaults to terraced_brushes; adaptive_surface approximates a smoother heightfield with finer brush cells in more complex areas.
Preview a local grayscale heightmap import without committing brushes.

Validate minimal TrenchBroom MCP scene IR without mutating the map. IR is a small JSON wrapper around existing atomic operations: operations for blockout_create_batch and entities for entity_create_checked_batch.
Preview minimal scene IR compile counts, parts, moduleId, and warnings without committing a transaction.

Read a local JSON IR file and preview the same minimal scene IR without mutating the map. Use this when generated IR would be too large for the conversation context. Successful valid previews return a session previewId that ir_apply_from_file can reuse without resending the path.
Apply minimal scene IR by dispatching to existing atomic MCP operations in transactions. This is an orchestration convenience for skill-generated IR, not a scene prefab.

Read a local JSON IR file and apply it through existing atomic MCP operations. The file is transport only; it does not add scene prefab semantics. Pass either path or a previewId returned by ir_compile_preview_from_file.
Create a curved corridor as one transaction using floor, ceiling, inner wall, outer wall, and optional caps.
Validate Blockout IR dimensions without modifying the map.
Create deterministic solid spiral stairs with matching center column and landing.
Analyze selected brush geometry for vertices, bounds, convexity, grid alignment, and materials.

Run native TrenchBroom CSG on the current selection. This is a selection-only boolean geometry primitive; prepare complex targets first with selection_set, objects_select_by_selector, or manual user selection.

Analyze live brush slope faces for ramp/wedge/surf/slide validation. Reports face normals, slope angle, rise direction, and whether each slope ascends or descends along routeDirection or start -> end. This is geometry/mapper semantics only, not gameplay difficulty analysis. Summary includes passed, slopeCount, warning samples, and recoveryAction. If operationIds, objectIds, and selector are omitted, analyzes the current user-selected brushes.

Analyze ordered route brush surfaces for playable continuity. Reports each target's upward playable face and each adjacent seam's verticalStep, horizontalGap, fullWidthContinuous, positiveGap, overlapDepth, and classification. edgeGapMax is retained as a legacy endpoint-distance metric and does not necessarily represent an empty seam. New workflows should use positiveGap, overlapDepth, and acceptancePassed. Summary includes passed, max gap/step fields, failing seam samples, and recoveryAction. Same-height overlaps are reported as overlap_continuous_height and remain continuous. If operationIds, objectIds, and selector are omitted, analyzes the current user-selected brushes.

Analyze annotated shell seam metadata on generated brush shells. This read-only validator groups brush metadata shellSeams by key and checks participant counts, shared vertex coordinates, and maxVertexDelta. It does not infer intended seams from arbitrary old map geometry; targets without shellSeams should be rebuilt with an annotated recipe or reviewed visually. If operationIds, objectIds, and selector are omitted, analyzes the current user-selected brushes.
Legacy object-id metadata setter. Prefer passing defaultMetadata/metadata to creation tools or using structured selectors/modules for recovery.
Legacy object-id metadata reader. Prefer selector_preview or module_inspect for structured metadata recovery.
Legacy metadata selector. Prefer structured selectors with selector_preview, objects_select_by_selector, objects_delete_by_selector, and render_review_selector.

Compatibility alias for route_geometry_analyze_chain. Returns geometric route facts only. Prefer geometry_analyze_route_continuity for route validation; difficulty should be judged by the Agent using project/domain context.

Analyze ordered brush-platform geometry facts such as edge gap, effective distance, height delta, lateral offset, and landing window area. This tool does not classify gameplay difficulty or pass/fail viability. Prefer geometry_analyze_route_continuity for current route validation workflows.
Validate selected spiral-stair brushes generated through MCP.
Search available TrenchBroom MCP tools by name, category, or description. Use detail=schema when exact parameters are needed.
